N0N-L1NERS: A Multimodal Video Retrieval System for CPU Execution

N0N-L1NERS answers text, image and speech queries over a large video collection, including ordered multi-event sequences, on a CPU only and with no LLM call in the temporal alignment.

Thien Huu Nguyen1,4*, Van Vinh Bui2,4*, Quang Minh Nguyen Tran1,4*, An Nguyen Hoang1,4*, Minh Hieu Phan1,4*, Minh-Huy Tran3,4, Nguyet Minh Nguyen Thi1, Loi Nguyen Khanh3,4

Search live. Keep the order.

Interactive benchmarks such as VBS, LSC and the Ho Chi Minh City AI Challenge expect answers at the speed of a live search, and some queries describe up to four events in a given order. Many systems call a remote vector database for every query, or rely on fixed time windows or LLM-based reranking, which either adds latency or limits the temporal structure a query can express.

N0N-L1NERS treats temporal alignment, query context and computational cost together. Embeddings stay in an in-memory FAISS index, keyframe information comes from Qdrant, and TRAKE aligns ordered events with a dynamic program that measures time gaps in seconds.

What “CPU-only” means

Retrieval and alignment run on a CPU, with no GPU needed at query time. Queries are still translated by an external API (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite), and memory grows with the number of keyframes.

Three query modes. One index.

Translate & shorten (≤77 tokens)→Encode text→Search FAISS→Top-50 keyframes

With a speech query, visual and ASR rankings are merged by Reciprocal Rank Fusion (c = 60).

SHA-256 hash of image→Exact hit? score 1.0→Else: encode image→Cosine on FAISS

An exact match returns the source keyframe without running the encoder; otherwise frames are ranked by embedding similarity.

Translate events & context→Blend vectors (w = 0.3)→DP per video→Ordered sequence ≤300 s

One keyframe per event from a single video, in the order of the query.

Design principles

Three ideas drive the system.

01

Blend the context, not the text

A shared context sentence is mixed into each event embedding (w = 0.3), so it costs none of the 77-token budget.

02

Exact match first

An image query tries an exact SHA-256 lookup first (score 1.0, no encoder run) and falls back to embedding similarity on a miss.

03

Align in seconds

TRAKE finds the best ordered chain per video with a linear-penalty dynamic program over timestamps, with no LLM call.

Interactive blueprint

From raw video to ordered events.

Select a block to inspect its role.

Offline indexing

TransNetV2 splits videos into shots and four keyframes are taken per shot. OpenCLIP ViT-H/14 (DFN-5B) encodes them; L2-normalized vectors go into a FAISS index. Keyframe info (video, frame ID, timestamp, path) is stored in Qdrant. The speech branch uses Whisper Large-v3 and EmbeddingGemma-300M.

Query processing

Vietnamese queries are translated and shortened by Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite to fit the 77-token limit of CLIP-style encoders, then encoded into a unit vector.

In-memory search

Embeddings are loaded in memory, so a query is one search in the FAISS index; keyframe info is read from Qdrant. The system returns the top-50 keyframes with no temporal constraint.

TRAKE alignment

The best chain per video maximizes total score minus λ times the summed time gaps (λ = 0.0008 per second), in O(L n log n). The Tmax = 300 s limit is checked after alignment. No new alignment algorithm is claimed: the linear-penalty formulation follows Luu et al. (2025).

Web interface

A FastAPI interface in Vietnamese and English shows ranked keyframes as thumbnails and submits answers to the DRES evaluation server.

Case studies

Three queries on the deployed system.

These are single queries that illustrate system behavior; they are not an evaluation.

The three top-1 frames lie in three different videos and cannot form a sequence. TRAKE returns L25_V088 at 18:19, 18:20, 18:23 (4 s), trading 0.11 of summed score (1.1166 → 1.0028) for the required order in one video.

The context biases results toward the intended scene without adding text tokens. Scores with and without context are not comparable.

One sequence from L22_V010 at 06:04, 06:16, 06:28, 06:29 (25 s). With λ = 0 the result is the same; the penalty is only 0.0008 × 25 = 0.02. A wider chain wins only if its extra similarity exceeds λΔ.

100 s → λΔ = 0.080

Measured on an Intel Core i5-7200U @ 2.50 GHz, medians over 50 queries. Final round of the Ho Chi Minh City AI Challenge 2026.

Scope and limitations

  • Ratings are the only quality measure; they are coarse and per task, allowing neither comparison with other systems nor attribution to components.
  • TRAKE received the lowest of the three ratings; w, λ and Tmax were not ablated.
  • Query translation depends on an external API, and memory grows with the number of keyframes.
